summary: Content Credentials record who made a piece of content and what was done to it, as signed statements bound to the bytes of the file. It is deployed rather than proposed: there is a conformance programme, a public list of conforming products, a published certificate policy and a curated list of trusted signing authorities. Two things a spatial computing group needs to know. First, no three-dimensional asset format appears anywhere in its list of supported formats, so a model cannot carry an embedded manifest at all; the byte-range binding works on any file, but the record has to travel beside the file as a separate manifest, and nothing keeps the two together. Second, the two pieces people most often credit to it are not in it: the verifiable credentials section and the training and data mining assertion were both removed from the core in version 2.0 of January 2024, and now live as separate specifications of another organisation. It records provenance; it does not enforce a licence, and its own principles say it passes no judgement on what it reports.

coverage.note: Statements about how an asset was made and changed are wrapped into a signed claim and tied to the asset by cryptographic hash.
